transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Well, I’m here because... for nearly two years now, I’ve been absolutely sure that our contractor and some of the people on my block have been quietly working together to cheat us. They're just keeping my kitchen half-wrong on purpose. My husband keeps showing me receipts, and they keep giving us all these excuses, but I know what's really going on.
Have you ever heard voices, seen things, or had any other unusual sensory experiences that other people don't seem to notice?

No, nothing like that. I don't... I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there, if that's what you mean. My mind is perfectly sound, doctor. I just see what is actually happening right in front of me with this house.

Aside from this situation with the contractor and neighbors, would you say you've generally had a hard time trusting people—like friends, family, or coworkers—for most of your life, even before this issue started?

No, I wouldn't say that at all. I've always been a pretty trusting person, really. I mean, I trust my husband, my friends... I never had any problems trusting the people I used to work with before I retired. So, no, it's not like I just go around suspecting everyone of things. 

It's just this specific situation with the house. I'm only suspicious of them because it's so obvious what they're doing to us.

Aside from this issue with the contractor, has your day-to-day functioning—things like your relationships, your ability to manage the household, or your usual activities—changed or declined at all over the past two years?

No, not at all. I mean... outside of dealing with this whole remodel mess, everything else is fine. I still keep up with my church gatherings, and my book club. I do all the normal household routines, you know, and we still make our family plans just the way we usually do. So, no, my day-to-day life hasn't really declined at all. Everything else is completely normal.

latest_inference.note: Preserved functioning across all domains, lifelong trusting personality, and an encapsulated, non-bizarre delusion focused solely on the contractor/neighbors argue against schizophrenia (F20.9), which requires broader functional decline or other psychotic symptoms. This narrows the picture toward Delusional Disorder (F22).

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a fixed, non-bizarre persecutory belief (that the contractor and neighbors are conspiring against her) lasting nearly two years. There are no hallucinations, no formal thought disorder, and no negative symptoms. Despite the delusion, her overall functioning (social, occupational, household) remains intact, and there is no pervasive lifelong pattern of distrust suggestive of a personality disorder. This clinical picture—an isolated, non-bizarre delusion without significant functional decline or other psychotic symptoms—is most consistent with Delusional Disorder (F22).
